sources.note: Koalib-Moro group-level, second-hand from Stevenson: 'dynamic Stress, accompanied by High or Low tone, plays a greater role than syllabic pitch as such, but is not equally prominent in all languages'; no placement rule and Lute is not among the varieties covered.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page lute1234 'Lute' and reference page 704642
sources.note: Nothing on stress; sole reference is Rosewood & Rosewood 2024 (listed by Glottolog as a wordlist + sociolinguistic); comment: Lute missing from Ethnologue E16-E28, spoken around Jebel Lute, 'not closely related to Koalib-Rere or any other Heibanic language'.

sources.note: Lute was previously counted as Koalib; Quint's dialect survey in the introduction may name the Hadra/Lute variety and his prosody chapters are the nearest full description in the cluster. Not a substitute for a Lute description (survey reports only 42% lexical similarity).
